Here is my thorough analysis of the tutors codebase.

---

## 1. Content Types / Learning Objects

The content model is defined in the `@tutors/tutors-model-lib` package. The canonical type lists are in:

**`D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/types/type-utils.ts`** (lines 18-43)

```typescript
export const simpleTypes = [
  "note", "archive", "web", "github", "panelnote", "paneltalk",
  "panelvideo", "podcast", "talk", "book", "lab", "tutorial",
];

export const loCompositeTypes = ["unit", "side", "topic", "course"];

export const loTypes: string[] = simpleTypes.concat(loCompositeTypes);
export type LoType = (typeof loTypes)[number];
```

**Simple (leaf) types:**
- **talk** -- A presentation/lecture with a PDF. Type defined at `learning-objects.ts:72-76`.
- **lab** -- Multi-step interactive lab with ordered `LabStep[]` entries and optional PDF. Type defined at `learning-objects.ts:61-66`.
- **note** -- Single-page markdown content. Type defined at `learning-objects.ts:115-117`.
- **tutorial** -- Text content with optional PDF. Type defined at `learning-objects.ts:105-109`.
- **archive** -- Downloadable file (zip, etc.). Type at `learning-objects.ts:82-85`.
- **web** -- External web link. Type at `learning-objects.ts:90-92`. Filtered out during tree decoration.
- **github** -- GitHub repository link. Type at `learning-objects.ts:97-99`.
- **paneltalk** -- Talk displayed inline as a panel. Type at `learning-objects.ts:138-140`.
- **panelnote** -- Note displayed inline as a panel. Type at `learning-objects.ts:131-133`.
- **panelvideo** -- Video displayed inline as a panel. Type at `learning-objects.ts:145-147`.
- **podcast** -- Spotify podcast embed. Type at `learning-objects.ts:123-126`.
- **book** -- Listed in `simpleTypes` but has no explicit TypeScript type definition (appears to be an alias/legacy name for lab steps).

**Composite (container) types:**
- **course** -- Top-level container. Type at `learning-objects.ts:206-232`. Has `loIndex`, `topicIndex`, `wallMap`, `properties`, `calendar`, `companions`, `wallBar`, etc.
- **topic** -- Groups related content under a theme. Type at `learning-objects.ts:182-184`.
- **unit** -- Major section within a topic. Type at `learning-objects.ts:189-191`.
- **side** -- Supplementary/sidebar content. Type at `learning-objects.ts:198-200`.

All composite types extend `Composite` (`learning-objects.ts:171-176`), which adds `toc: Lo[]`, `los: Lo[]`, `panels: Panels`, and `units: Units`.

The base `Lo` type (`learning-objects.ts:14-40`) is the core type for all content, with fields: `type`, `id`, `title`, `summary`, `contentMd`, `contentHtml`, `route`, `authLevel`, `img`, `video`, `videoids`, `hide`, `parentLo`, `parentTopic`, `parentCourse`, `breadCrumbs`, `frontMatter`, `icon`, `learningRecords`.

There is also a display ordering map (`preOrder` in `type-utils.ts:63-80`) that ranks types for sorting.

**All type definition files (in the model library):**
- `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/types/learning-objects.ts`
- `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/types/type-utils.ts`
- `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/types/icon-types.ts`
- `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/types/media-types.ts`
- `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/types/calendar-types.ts`

---

## 2. Route Structure and Rendering

All reader routes live under `src/routes/(course-reader)/`. The route group layout provides a shared shell. Route patterns:

| Route pattern | Content type | Svelte component used |
|---|---|---|
| `/course/[courseid]` | Course (composite) | `Composite.svelte` |
| `/topic/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Topic (composite) | `Composite.svelte` |
| `/lab/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Lab (multi-step) | `Lab.svelte` (or `TalkClient.svelte` if lab has PDF) |
| `/talk/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Talk (PDF presentation) | `TalkClient.svelte` inside `Context.svelte` |
| `/paneltalk/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Panel talk | `TalkClient.svelte` inside `Context.svelte` |
| `/note/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Note (markdown) | `Note.svelte` inside `Context.svelte` |
| `/tutorial/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Tutorial (markdown + optional PDF) | `Note.svelte` + conditional `TalkClient.svelte` |
| `/video/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Video | `Video.svelte` inside `Context.svelte` |
| `/wall/[type]/[courseid]` | Wall (all items of a type) | `Wall.svelte` |
| `/search/[courseid]` | Search | Search page |
| `/llm/[courseid]` | LLM chat | LLM page |
| `/time/[courseid]` | Time tracking | Time page |

**How rendering is decided:**
- Each route has a `+page.ts` data loader that calls `courseService` methods (`readCourse`, `readTopic`, `readLab`, `readLo`, `readWall`).
- The `+page.svelte` receives the loaded data and renders a specific component based on the route.
- For composite types (course, topic), the `Composite.svelte` component recursively renders `Panels` (panelvideos, paneltalks, panelnotes, podcasts), `Units` (unit/side composites), and `Cards` (standard leaf LOs).
- For leaf content, `Context.svelte` wraps the content with a sidebar showing sibling LOs from the parent topic.
- The lab page has a special case: if the lab has a `pdf` property, it renders `TalkClient` (PDF viewer) instead of the step-by-step `Lab` component.

**Key UI component files:**
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/structure/Composite.svelte` -- renders composite LOs
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/structure/Context.svelte` -- wraps leaf LOs with context sidebar
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/content/Lab.svelte` -- multi-step lab renderer
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/content/Note.svelte` -- markdown note renderer
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/content/Video.svelte` -- video embed (YouTube, HEAnet, VIMP)
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/content/TalkClient.svelte` -- PDF viewer (Adobe or Mozilla)
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/content/Podcast.svelte` -- Spotify embed
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Card.svelte` -- card component for LO listings
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Cards.svelte` -- grid of cards
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Panels.svelte` -- inline panel content
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Units.svelte` -- unit/side sections
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Wall.svelte` -- wall view (all LOs of a type)

## 3. Markdown Rendering

Markdown is rendered using **markdown-it** (not marked, remark, or mdsvex). The rendering pipeline has two layers:

**Layer 1: Model library (`@tutors/tutors-model-lib`)**

File: `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/utils/markdown-utils.ts`

The core markdown-it instance is configured with these plugins:
- `markdown-it-katex` -- LaTeX math rendering
- `markdown-it-anchor` -- Header anchor links
- `markdown-it-table-of-contents` -- TOC generation (levels 1-3)
- `markdown-it-emoji` -- Emoji shortcodes
- `markdown-it-sub` -- Subscript
- `markdown-it-sup` -- Superscript
- `markdown-it-mark` -- Highlight marks
- `markdown-it-footnote` -- Footnotes
- `markdown-it-deflist` -- Definition lists
- Custom `videoPlayer` plugin -- handles `::video[src='...' ...]::` syntax for inline video embeds
- Custom `podcastPlayer` plugin -- handles `::podcast[src='...' ...]::` syntax for Spotify embeds
- Custom `link_open` renderer -- opens external links in new tabs
- Custom `blockquote_open/close` renderers -- styled blockquotes

Code highlighting uses **Shiki** (passed in via `initHighlighter()`). The `highlight` function in the markdown-it config calls `shiki.codeToHtml()` with the current theme.

Key functions:
- `convertMdToHtml(md, codeTheme)` -- converts raw markdown string to HTML
- `convertLoToHtml(course, lo)` -- converts any LO's markdown, handling labs, notes, and general LOs differently
- `filter(src, url, protocol)` -- rewrites relative image/archive paths to absolute URLs before rendering

**Layer 2: App-level markdown service**

File: `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/markdown/services/markdown.svelte.ts`

This service initializes the Shiki highlighter synchronously using `createHighlighterCoreSync` with:
- 31 programming languages (JS, TS, Python, Java, Kotlin, C#, Go, Rust, R, Haskell, Scala, Svelte, Vue, and more)
- 7 themes (ayu-dark, monokai, github-dark, night-owl, solarized-light, github-light, catppuccin-latte)

It provides:
- `convertLabToHtml(course, lab, refreshOnly)` -- processes lab summary and each step's markdown
- `convertNoteToHtml(course, note, refreshOnly)` -- processes note markdown
- `setCodeTheme(theme)` -- persists user's preferred syntax highlighting theme

**Where HTML is rendered in the UI:**
- `Note.svelte` renders `{@html lo.contentHtml}` inside `<article class="prose dark:prose-invert">`.
- `Lab.svelte` renders `{@html lab.content}` (the current step's HTML) inside `<article class="prose dark:prose-invert">`.
- Both include KaTeX CSS from CDN for math rendering.
- Tailwind Typography's `prose` class handles markdown HTML styling.

**Markdown-related files:**
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/markdown/services/markdown.svelte.ts`
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/markdown/types.ts`
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/markdown/index.ts`
- `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/utils/markdown-utils.ts`
- `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/utils/markdown-plugins.ts`

## 4. Data Fetching and Parsing

**Course data fetching:**

File: `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/course.svelte.ts`

The flow is:
1. A route's `+page.ts` calls `courseService.readCourse(courseId, fetch)` (or `readTopic`, `readLab`, `readLo`, `readWall`).
2. `readCourse` calls `getOrLoadCourse`, which checks a `Map<string, Course>` cache.
3. If not cached, it calls `determineCourseUrl(courseId)` (in `lo-tree.ts`) to resolve the course ID into a URL. Rules: if it looks like a full URL, use it directly; if it starts with `192` or `localhost`, use HTTP; otherwise, append `.netlify.app`.
4. It fetches `{protocol}{courseUrl}/tutors.json` -- this is the **single JSON file containing the entire course tree**.
5. The JSON is cast to `Course` type (the JSON structure must match the `Course`/`Lo` type hierarchy).
6. `decorateCourseTree(course, courseId, courseUrl)` is called to post-process the tree.

**Tree decoration (post-processing):**

File: `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/lo-tree.ts` (app-level version)
File: `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/services/lo-tree.ts` (library version)

`decorateCourseTree` does:
1. Sets `courseId`, `courseUrl`, and `route` on the course.
2. `flattenLos()` recursively collects all LOs into a flat array.
3. `injectCourseUrl()` replaces `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholders in routes, images, videos, and PDFs with actual URLs.
4. `removeUnknownLos()` strips LOs with type "unknown".
5. `decorateLoTree()` recursively walks the tree, setting `parentCourse`, loading icons from frontmatter, building breadcrumbs, converting markdown to HTML (except labs and notes which are deferred), and for composite LOs, splitting children into `panels` (panelvideos, paneltalks, panelnotes, podcasts) and `units` (units, sides, standardLos).
6. Builds `loIndex` (a `Map<string, Lo>` keyed by route) and `topicIndex`.
7. `loadPropertyFlags()` reads course properties (portfolio, private, auth level, PDF reader, etc.).
8. `createCompanions()` builds the companion navigation bar (Slack, Zoom, Moodle, YouTube, Teams, Podcast links from properties).
9. `createWalls()` groups LOs by type into walls for the wall view. Wall types: `["talk", "tutorial", "note", "lab", "podcast", "web", "archive", "github"]`.
10. `initCalendar()` parses course calendar data if present.

**Lab and note conversion on demand:**

Labs and notes have their markdown converted lazily (not during initial tree decoration) because they can be expensive:
- `courseService.readLab()` calls `markdownService.convertLabToHtml(course, lab)` then creates a `LiveLab` instance.
- `courseService.readLo()` calls `markdownService.convertNoteToHtml(course, note)` when `lo.type === "note"`.

**LiveLab class:**

File: `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/live-lab.ts`

Manages lab state: builds a map from step short-titles to their HTML content, handles step navigation (next/prev/setActive), generates the sidebar navigation HTML, and supports keyboard navigation (arrow keys).

**Key data-fetching files:**
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/course.svelte.ts` -- main course service
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/lo-tree.ts` -- tree decoration
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/live-lab.ts` -- lab state management
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/types.ts` -- CourseService and LabService interfaces
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/index.ts` -- re-exports
- `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/runes.svelte.ts` -- global reactive state (currentCourse, currentLo, etc.)

## 2. Route Structure and Rendering

All reader routes live under `src/routes/(course-reader)/`. The route group layout provides a shared shell. Route patterns:

| Route pattern | Content type | Svelte component used |
|---|---|---|
| `/course/[courseid]` | Course (composite) | `Composite.svelte` |
| `/topic/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Topic (composite) | `Composite.svelte` |
| `/lab/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Lab (multi-step) | `Lab.svelte` (or `TalkClient.svelte` if lab has PDF) |
| `/talk/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Talk (PDF presentation) | `TalkClient.svelte` inside `Context.svelte` |
| `/paneltalk/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Panel talk | `TalkClient.svelte` inside `Context.svelte` |
| `/note/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Note (markdown) | `Note.svelte` inside `Context.svelte` |
| `/tutorial/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Tutorial (markdown + optional PDF) | `Note.svelte` + conditional `TalkClient.svelte` |
| `/video/[courseid]/[...loid]` | Video | `Video.svelte` inside `Context.svelte` |
| `/wall/[type]/[courseid]` | Wall (all items of a type) | `Wall.svelte` |
| `/search/[courseid]` | Search | Search page |
| `/llm/[courseid]` | LLM chat | LLM page |
| `/time/[courseid]` | Time tracking | Time page |

**How rendering is decided:**
- Each route has a `+page.ts` data loader that calls `courseService` methods (`readCourse`, `readTopic`, `readLab`, `readLo`, `readWall`).
- The `+page.svelte` receives the loaded data and renders a specific component based on the route.
- For composite types (course, topic), the `Composite.svelte` component recursively renders `Panels` (panelvideos, paneltalks, panelnotes, podcasts), `Units` (unit/side composites), and `Cards` (standard leaf LOs).
- For leaf content, `Context.svelte` wraps the content with a sidebar showing sibling LOs from the parent topic.
- The lab page has a special case: if the lab has a `pdf` property, it renders `TalkClient` (PDF viewer) instead of the step-by-step `Lab` component.

## 3. Markdown Rendering

Markdown is rendered using **markdown-it** (not marked, remark, or mdsvex). The rendering pipeline has two layers:

**Layer 1: Model library (`@tutors/tutors-model-lib`)**

File: `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/utils/markdown-utils.ts`

The core markdown-it instance is configured with these plugins:
- `markdown-it-katex` -- LaTeX math rendering
- `markdown-it-anchor` -- Header anchor links
- `markdown-it-table-of-contents` -- TOC generation (levels 1-3)
- `markdown-it-emoji` -- Emoji shortcodes
- `markdown-it-sub` -- Subscript
- `markdown-it-sup` -- Superscript
- `markdown-it-mark` -- Highlight marks
- `markdown-it-footnote` -- Footnotes
- `markdown-it-deflist` -- Definition lists
- Custom `videoPlayer` plugin -- handles `::video[src='...' ...]::` syntax for inline video embeds
- Custom `podcastPlayer` plugin -- handles `::podcast[src='...' ...]::` syntax for Spotify embeds
- Custom `link_open` renderer -- opens external links in new tabs
- Custom `blockquote_open/close` renderers -- styled blockquotes

Code highlighting uses **Shiki** (passed in via `initHighlighter()`). The `highlight` function in the markdown-it config calls `shiki.codeToHtml()` with the current theme.

Key functions:
- `convertMdToHtml(md, codeTheme)` -- converts raw markdown string to HTML
- `convertLoToHtml(course, lo)` -- converts any LO's markdown, handling labs, notes, and general LOs differently
- `filter(src, url, protocol)` -- rewrites relative image/archive paths to absolute URLs before rendering

**Layer 2: App-level markdown service**

File: `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/markdown/services/markdown.svelte.ts`

This service initializes the Shiki highlighter synchronously using `createHighlighterCoreSync` with:
- 31 programming languages (JS, TS, Python, Java, Kotlin, C#, Go, Rust, R, Haskell, Scala, Svelte, Vue, and more)
- 7 themes (ayu-dark, monokai, github-dark, night-owl, solarized-light, github-light, catppuccin-latte)

It provides:
- `convertLabToHtml(course, lab, refreshOnly)` -- processes lab summary and each step's markdown
- `convertNoteToHtml(course, note, refreshOnly)` -- processes note markdown
- `setCodeTheme(theme)` -- persists user's preferred syntax highlighting theme

**Where HTML is rendered in the UI:**
- `Note.svelte` renders `{@html lo.contentHtml}` inside `<article class="prose dark:prose-invert">`.
- `Lab.svelte` renders `{@html lab.content}` (the current step's HTML) inside `<article class="prose dark:prose-invert">`.
- Both include KaTeX CSS from CDN for math rendering.
- Tailwind Typography's `prose` class handles markdown HTML styling.

## 4. Data Fetching and Parsing

**Course data fetching:**

File: `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/course.svelte.ts`

The flow is:
1. A route's `+page.ts` calls `courseService.readCourse(courseId, fetch)` (or `readTopic`, `readLab`, `readLo`, `readWall`).
2. `readCourse` calls `getOrLoadCourse`, which checks a `Map<string, Course>` cache.
3. If not cached, it calls `determineCourseUrl(courseId)` (in `lo-tree.ts`) to resolve the course ID into a URL. Rules: if it looks like a full URL, use it directly; if it starts with `192` or `localhost`, use HTTP; otherwise, append `.netlify.app`.
4. It fetches `{protocol}{courseUrl}/tutors.json` -- this is the **single JSON file containing the entire course tree**.
5. The JSON is cast to `Course` type (the JSON structure must match the `Course`/`Lo` type hierarchy).
6. `decorateCourseTree(course, courseId, courseUrl)` is called to post-process the tree.

**Tree decoration (post-processing):**

File: `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/lo-tree.ts` (app-level version)
File: `D:/code/tutors/node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/services/lo-tree.ts` (library version)

`decorateCourseTree` does:
1. Sets `courseId`, `courseUrl`, and `route` on the course.
2. `flattenLos()` recursively collects all LOs into a flat array.
3. `injectCourseUrl()` replaces `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholders in routes, images, videos, and PDFs with actual URLs.
4. `removeUnknownLos()` strips LOs with type "unknown".
5. `decorateLoTree()` recursively walks the tree, setting `parentCourse`, loading icons from frontmatter, building breadcrumbs, converting markdown to HTML (except labs and notes which are deferred), and for composite LOs, splitting children into `panels` (panelvideos, paneltalks, panelnotes, podcasts) and `units` (units, sides, standardLos).
6. Builds `loIndex` (a `Map<string, Lo>` keyed by route) and `topicIndex`.
7. `loadPropertyFlags()` reads course properties (portfolio, private, auth level, PDF reader, etc.).
8. `createCompanions()` builds the companion navigation bar (Slack, Zoom, Moodle, YouTube, Teams, Podcast links from properties).
9. `createWalls()` groups LOs by type into walls for the wall view. Wall types: `["talk", "tutorial", "note", "lab", "podcast", "web", "archive", "github"]`.
10. `initCalendar()` parses course calendar data if present.

**Lab and note conversion on demand:**

Labs and notes have their markdown converted lazily (not during initial tree decoration) because they can be expensive:
- `courseService.readLab()` calls `markdownService.convertLabToHtml(course, lab)` then creates a `LiveLab` instance.
- `courseService.readLo()` calls `markdownService.convertNoteToHtml(course, note)` when `lo.type === "note"`.

**LiveLab class:**

File: `D:/code/tutors/src/lib/services/course/services/live-lab.ts`

Manages lab state: builds a map from step short-titles to their HTML content, handles step navigation (next/prev/setActive), generates the sidebar navigation HTML, and supports keyboard navigation (arrow keys).
